148d5a4852.q: What experiential hospitality experiences does Elevate offer at the U.S. Open tennis tournament?
148d5a4852.a: Elevate offers U.S. Open experiences that include arrival in an official US Open Cadillac with concierge guidance through crowds, access to exclusive hospitality space with premier food and beverage, front row baseline seating, in-seat service to avoid missing play, meet-and-greets with former players and champions, and the ability to play tennis with Andre Agassi and Arthur Ashe, plus trophy pictures. The in-seat service was created specifically because in tennis, walking the concourse or stairs distracts players, so drinks and food are brought directly to attendees.

16185892dc.q: How does Elevate convince sports leagues and events to outsource hospitality and premium access instead of keeping it exclusive to sponsors?
16185892dc.a: Dan Rosenthal explains that Elevate must convince rights holders on multiple fronts: first, that outsourcing creates incremental commercial value beyond standard tickets; second, that providing access to paying customers is beneficial rather than keeping it exclusive; and third, that fans will actually pay significant dollars above normal ticket prices for these curated experiences. The challenge involves aligning with operational teams to ensure seamless execution while remaining authentic to each specific event rather than repeating the same formula across different properties.

37d31fb2e8.q: What was Dan Rosenthal's early struggle in sales and how did he overcome it?
37d31fb2e8.a: Rosenthal was the worst salesperson initially but compensated by outworking everyone—being first in and last out, making more phone calls than anyone else. His breakthrough came when a senior colleague advised him to infuse his personality and understand rhythm like music, rather than reading scripts word for word. By understanding the beats and notes of a sales conversation, he was able to freestyle within the framework instead of following exact words, which transformed his sales performance into being one of the top sellers for four to five straight years.

c14f875b64.q: Why did the New York Yankees need to build an outbound sales culture when Dan Rosenthal joined in 2009?
c14f875b64.a: The Yankees had not had a full outbound sales culture or inside sales team before Rosenthal arrived. When the new stadium opened in 2009, the economy crashed, forcing the organization to change their business model. Rosenthal was brought in post-stadium opening to create an outbound B2B sales environment and build an entry-level sales team from scratch, as the organization had primarily relied on the brand value of winning baseball games rather than proactive revenue generation.
